cards.body:
## Summary
The set of metrics a Linga journey is judged on is written out five times in uat/driver, and the copies already disagree. Make one registry the only place a metric is declared; the judge schema, the gates, the roll-up, the before/after delta and the report are derived from it.

## Description
The verdict, ledger and recertify work moved the decision into code, and in doing so each module re-listed the metrics it needs. The judge is asked for five metric groups (linga-text.cjs:76-82). verdict.cjs can gate six series (:71-78) and cannot gate judge agreement. recertify.cjs rolls up and deltas seven (:53-77). The report prints six bullets (:313-318). Moment recall is asked, stored, and read by nothing. Check length is in the rubric and in J1's measures list and exists nowhere in code. A gate with a typo is found only after the run.

The move is a new uat/driver/metrics.cjs: each entry declares its judge key, the JSON schema of that key, and its series (id, label, an of(record) that returns [numerator, denominator], and how a gate reads it). placement stays special only in that its of() reads record.facts.placement.class. linga-text.cjs builds the metrics half of judgeSchema from the registry; verdict.cjs gateReason() reads series by id; recertify.cjs rollUp() and metricDelta() fold over series; synthesize() and characterReport() print one line per series. A journey's gates are validated against the registry when the runner starts. The judge schema stays byte-identical for the existing metrics (case 1 pins it), so no prompt, finding or committed run changes; the one visible change is that moment recall is finally reported.

A second module's metric (Math Buddy's hint withholding, marking agreement) then becomes one registry entry instead of five edits across three files.

## Flow
- Operator adds a metric: one entry in metrics.cjs and, if it should gate, one line in a journey's gates.
- Run start: unknownGates() checks every journey file; a typo stops the run before any model call.
- Judge answers, verdictOf() gates it, rollUp()/metricDelta() track it across reruns, report.md prints it. No other edit.

## Expected impact
Operators: a verdict, a delta and a report row can no longer disagree about what a metric is, and a metric the rubric promises (recall) shows up. Builders: the next module's UAT is a registry entry, not a five-file hunt. Counted: 5 hand-kept lists collapse to 1, 1 asked-but-unread metric becomes read, 1 rubric metric with no code is named as driver-measured instead of silently absent.

## Evaluation
Claim: the metric set is declared once, and the schema, gates, roll-up, delta and report are derived from it without changing any existing output.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (cases 2-7; cases 1 and 8 are guards, green before by design)
After: 6 of 6, guards still green
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none

acceptance: case 1: product.surface() -> a sorted, repo-relative list of the desk/src files the driver loads (the entry modules of linga-text.cjs/surface.cjs read back from require.cache after one surfaceOf render): includes desk/src/lib/english/view.ts, desk/src/english/LingaPhone.tsx, desk/src/lib/english/placement.ts; excludes anything under node_modules and desk/data; identical on a second call; at least 40 files (tools/uat-ledger-test.cjs, node:test; the module does not exist yet)

case 3 (GUARD, green before by design): two run.json files with the same instrument and different product stamps -> confounds() lists 0 confounds of kind 'instrument'; the product lives beside instrument in run.json, never inside it, so a product change is never read as an instrument change (tools/uat-recertify-test.cjs)

case 5: a run whose run.json carries product.files -> the ledger reads the stamp and makes no git call (the injected git runner throws if called); a run with neither stamp nor git history is seen null and is counted separately as 'unknown', never as current (tools/uat-ledger-test.cjs)

case 7: renderRecertify() for a before and an after run whose product.files are identical, with a code-verdict drop on one pair -> that pair is listed under 'Confounded - do not read as a regression' with 'product unchanged in 63 files: run-to-run noise' and not under Regressed; the same drop with 2 files changed lists the pair under Regressed and the row names the 2 files; with no stamp on either side and no git history the Confounded table carries the note 'product not recorded' (tools/uat-recertify-test.cjs)

cards.body:
## Summary
OPEN.md says '186 open'. Every one of those rows was seen on a product in which 60 of the 63 files the driver loads have since changed, and the operator is not told. Stamp the product into every run, derive the same stamp from git for the old ones, and let OPEN.md and recertify.md say what is still seen on the current product, what is only old, and when a rerun's verdict change cannot be the product.

## Description
The overlay already records what instrument produced a run (model, efforts, screen cap, driver hashes) so that a driver change cannot pass for a product change. It never records the other half: which product the run exercised. The consequence is on the operator's screen today. uat/runs/OPEN.md reports 186 open rows in 36 pairs, drained 0 of 5, as if they were one backlog; the rows come from five runs committed on 15 Sep, and 135 commits to the files those runs loaded (60 of 63 changed) have landed since. Nothing separates a gap still present from one a later commit probably removed, and the only way to find out is the 36-pair recertify (about 30-50 model calls a pair). In the other direction, a recertify whose verdict drops on byte-identical product code is a measurement of judge and Character noise, but recertify.md has no way to say so and files it under Regressed.

The move: uat/driver/product.cjs derives the load set (the desk/src files in require.cache after the driver's entry modules load and one surface renders; no hand-kept list), stamps { commit, dirty, files: { path: blob sha } } into run.json beside instrument (never inside it, or a product change would read as an instrument confound), and answers seenOf(run) for a run without a stamp from git: the commit that first added the run's findings.json, with git ls-tree blobs compared to the working tree. The ledger gives each gap seen and changed; OPEN.md leads with the split and ends each row with 'product: N of 63 files changed since'. renderRecertify compares the two product stamps: identical means a verdict change is noise and is listed as confounded; different means it can be read as a product change and names the files. A run with neither stamp nor history is 'unknown', never current.

It asks for no new typing and no new run: it changes what the operator KNOWS from files and git already there. It is deliberately not a gap-to-file mapping (finding code_hint is empty on all 186 rows); it states a fact the repo can prove, product changed or not, and leaves attribution to the drain.

## Flow
- Operator runs `node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --status`: OPEN.md opens with '186 open: 0 seen on the current product, 186 seen before a product change', each row ends with its own changed-file count.
- Operator runs any new run: run.json carries product; the next --status counts those rows as current until the product moves again.
- Operator runs a recertify: recertify.md says whether the product moved between the two runs; a drop on an unmoved product is shown as noise, a drop on a moved one as Regressed with the changed files named.

## Expected impact
The drain starts from an honest number: 186 rows become '0 current, 186 aged' instead of a flat backlog, and the first live run since 25 Sep (none exists on the verdict and instrument code) will be the first to give a current figure. Every future recertify becomes either a fix check or a free noise measurement, which the single-sample verdicts have lacked. Counted: 1 recorded fact added per run, 3 operator surfaces change (OPEN.md header, row suffix, recertify.md Confounded), 0 model calls added.

## Evaluation
Claim: the ledger and the recertify report state, from files and git alone, whether the product a finding was seen on has changed, and a verdict change on an unchanged product is reported as noise.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (cases 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7; cases 3 and 8 are guards, green before by design)
After: 6 of 6, guards still green
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none
